edits.old: The synthetic promise amount 12500 is the monthly instalment of the worked example in the Temporal and Drools design, used as a fixture value and not as a business parameter.
edits.new: The synthetic promise amount 12500 is the monthly instalment of the worked example in the Temporal and Drools design, used as a fixture value and not as a business parameter. The harness reads no ACE view directly; it reads the DP02 and DP05 records through the rwb-source-data contract. The cutover extract is a one-off read of the legacy cutover dump with the legacy record key as its idempotency key, and its record format, file name, the identity that reads it, and the cutover record holding the counts, the ten day rows and the sign-off are fixed at the cutover rehearsal and recorded in this story's Flyway description (GAP-0526). The migrated interaction keeps person_key and contact_key as ACE business keys and carries no party_id or contact_point_id of its own (GAP-0527). The DM-005 cutover load writes the legacy consent and contact-quality rows into contact_point_ext; RWB-P1-DM002-APP reads them for DP02 and writes none (GAP-0528). Open promises and contact notes land in rwb_source_data.interaction, with the consent flags in contact_point_ext, and EFS history stays a read through v_ace_efs_action (GAP-0243).

edits.old: The extract format, its retention and the report shape are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0445; ASM-0637).
edits.new: The harness pack is agreed at the wave 4 entry check by the Integration lead, which fixes the SIT hosts, a cutover extract fixture of one case and two contact keys, a break list of one row per orphan with key type, key value, reason and owner role, the extract format and retention, the gate signature, the seeding set, and the no-copy assertion on the interaction source and migrated_at with a zero count of EFS-shaped ledger rows (GAP-0445; ASM-0637).
